challenges.name: duplicate-side-effects
challenges.title: Certificate emails sent twice: what stops the duplicate
challenges.description: A learner received the same certificate email twice after a worker was stopped between sending the email and writing "sent". Two statements on the worker code and its logs ask which change actually prevents the second email.

questions.explanation: False. A database transaction can only roll back what the database did. The email left through the provider's API at 10:14:02.118, before the process died; rolling back the status update leaves it at pending, which is exactly the state that made worker c07 send again. Wrapping the send in a transaction even makes things slightly worse: the transaction stays open during a network call. The misconception is that a transaction makes any block of code atomic; side effects outside the database need their own protection: an idempotency key the provider honours, or a marker written before the side effect with a rule for what to do when the marker is found.

True. The key names the side effect ("the certificate email for cert_7781"), so every delivery of the job uses the same key and the provider delivers once and answers the second call as a duplicate. The key must not include the job attempt, the receive count or a timestamp: then every redelivery has a new key and the provider sends again. The limit is the window: after 24 h the provider forgets the key, which is why the worker also writes a marker before sending and does not resend automatically when it finds an old claim.

challenges.name: certificate-emails-sent-twice
challenges.title: Certificate emails sent twice
challenges.description: Since the CodeDev workers moved to spot instances, some learners get their certificate email two or three times. The queue delivers at least once: a worker that dies after sending the email but before writing "sent" leaves the job to be delivered again, and a worker slower than the visibility timeout sees a second worker pick up the same job while it is still running. Fix sendCertificateEmail(job, ctx) so each certificate email is delivered once, following this protocol. key = "certificate-email/<certId>", the same for every delivery of that certificate. 1) Read the certificate with ctx.db.get; if it is unknown (null), "sent" or "needs-review", do nothing. 2) If it is "pending", claim it with ctx.db.update(id, "pending", { status: "sending", claimedAt: ctx.now() }); update is a compare-and-set that returns false when the status is no longer "pending" - in either case read the certificate again and continue from step 1 with the new status. 3) If it is "sending" and ctx.now() - claimedAt < 86400 (24 h), send it with ctx.email.send({ to, template: "certificate-issued", certId, idempotencyKey: key }), then ctx.db.update(id, "sending", { status: "sent" }) (a false result is fine: another worker finished first). 4) If it is "sending" and ctx.now() - claimedAt >= 86400, do not send - the provider no longer remembers the key, so a resend could reach the learner twice; set ctx.db.update(id, "sending", { status: "needs-review" }) for a person to check the provider's log. The email provider fake delivers at most once per idempotencyKey within 24 h (a send whose key was delivered less than 86,400 s earlier returns "duplicate" and delivers nothing; without a key it always delivers). Input: { certificates, script }; the script plays the broker: { at, deliver, cert, crashAfter?, pauseAfter? } starts a worker on a delivery, { at, resume } lets a paused worker continue; crashAfter/pauseAfter name an operation ("get", "update", "send") after whose first call, once it has taken effect, the worker dies (never continues) or pauses. Output: emails delivered per learner, the final status of every certificate, and worker errors. Do not change the fakes or the test runner.
hints: List every point where the worker can stop: after reading, after sending, after writing. For each one, what does the next delivery of the same job find in the database, and what does it do? Which of those points produces a second email today?

Two things must change in sendCertificateEmail: the database must say "someone has started this" before the email is sent (the claim, with the time), and the email must carry a key that is the same for every delivery of the certificate. Then decide, from the status and claimedAt you read, whether to claim, send, give up or flag.

A similar protocol for a different side effect - charging a course purchase: key = "purchase-charge/ord_17"; mark the order "charging" with chargingAt = now only if it is "created"; when you find it "charging" within the payment provider's dedupe window, charge again with the same key (the provider answers with the first charge) and mark it "charged"; outside the window, mark it "needs-review" instead of charging again.

tests.name: One delivery per certificate: one email per learner and status sent
Worker dies after the email, the job is delivered again 60 s later: still one email
Slower than the visibility timeout: B runs while A is paused after sending, then A resumes
Two workers read the same pending certificate before either of them claims it
Worker dies after the claim, before the email: the redelivery sends it exactly once
Redelivery 24 h or more after the claim is never resent: needs-review; just under 24 h is deduped
Unknown, already sent and needs-review certificates send nothing, even when delivered 3 times
Large input: 150 certificates with crashes, pauses, races and late redeliveries
